about: A 28 kg dog's muscles for dog_anat.xml (make_muscles.py dog). Main-swing strength per joint group in N m; out-of-plane hinges get a share of it. Fixed 2026-11-21 before the anat_dog run.

sources.hindlimb: Williams SB, Usherwood JR, Jespers K, Channon AJ, Wilson AM (2009) Exploring the mechanical basis for acceleration: pelvic limb locomotor function during accelerations in racing greyhounds. J Exp Biol 212:550-565, doi:10.1242/jeb.018093, Fig. 9: peak net extensor moments at high acceleration in a 28.5 kg greyhound, hip ~40, stifle ~25, tarsus ~45 N m (inverse dynamics). Strength here = 1.4 x those peaks (a gallop runs muscles below their isometric force; 1.3-1.5x).
sources.check: Ellis RG, Rankin JW, Hutchinson JR (2018) Front Bioeng Biotechnol 6:162, doi:10.3389/fbioe.2018.00162, Table 2: gastrocnemius PCSA 38.4 cm2, Fmax 925 N; at a ~4.5 cm calcaneal lever ~42 N m from that muscle alone, consistent with 63 N m for all tarsal extensors. Table 4: sit-to-stand peaks hip 13.6, stifle 4.8, tarsus 12.9 N m (27 kg greyhound).
sources.forelimb_spine_neck_head: ESTIMATES: no published inverse dynamics found for the canine forelimb at maximal effort, nor for spine, neck or head. Forelimb set from the hindlimb counterparts (shoulder as hip; elbow between stifle and tarsus, the triceps being large; carpus below tarsus, its stance load carried largely by palmar ligaments and flexor tendons) and the forelimb's share of support (about 60% of body weight standing; up to 4.5x body weight per forelimb landing from a jump, Pfau T et al. 2011 Vet J). The thoracic sling (scapula on the thorax) carries that support.
sources.activation: Zajac FE (1989) Crit Rev Biomed Eng 17:359-411: activation 10 ms, deactivation 40 ms (the default of published quadruped musculoskeletal models, Ellis 2018 included). One time constant here (a target move activates one muscle of a pair and relaxes the other): 25 ms.
sources.speed: No per-joint gallop speeds are published, and galloping dogs reach theirs partly through tendon recoil, which this body lacks. Each joint's zero-force speed is 3x the fastest the capture's dog reached (99.9th percentile of the main swing over the capture), so the body can still do what the dog did; at that speed its muscles keep about 29% of their strength (Hill, curvature 0.25).
